Canada · CPA certification · 2026 to 2029

CPA certification: the current program and its 2027 replacementW13

A working guide to both programs. Part A covers the current program (CPA PEP and the Common Final Examination), which ends Dec 31, 2028.W13 Part B covers the new CPA Professional Program. Each is described the same way: structure, exams, how Ontario, Quebec, the West and Atlantic Canada run it, dates, experience and cost.

Compiled Nov 17, 2026 Every citation re-checked Nov 18, 2026 Official CPA sources; university pages in red 140 sources, cited inline Reading copy

Each body’s pages said that details of the new program were still being developed, not yet available or subject to change.W7ON4QC2A1 What had not been published is listed in Open items.

Part AThe current programCPA PEP, the Common Final Examination and practical experience. Last intake January 2027; ends Dec 31, 2028.W13W13

01The current program at a glance

The current program was developed nationally and is delivered by provincial or regional bodies, with CPA Canada setting the exam dates and marking all exams. Six modules lead to one three-day exam, with practical experience running alongside.W33W28BC1W22

6modules: two core, two elective, two capstoneW22
4module exams of four hours eachW28W29
13hCommon Final Examination, over three days (4 + 5 + 4 hours, our sum)W21
30moof practical experience (24 in Quebec)W24QC9
16–24momost common time to finish the six modulesW29A10
6yrlimit for the modules and CFE in the West, Ontario and AtlanticW23ON23A10

What to know first

  • National exams, regional delivery. CPA Canada sets the exam dates and marks every exam; provincial or regional bodies deliver the program. In the West, CPAWSB delivers CPA PEP and the provincial bodies administer the experience requirements.W28BC1W33
  • Everything builds to one exam. Candidates must complete all six modules before writing the three-day CFE.W22
  • The electives carry the specialization. Two of four are chosen, and Assurance plus Taxation is the public accounting route.W22ON21
  • Experience runs separately. The 30 months can be finished before or after the CFE, within the time limit.W16
  • It closes module by module. Each module has a dated final offering, ending with the last CFE on Sep 26–28, 2028.W25

The path in one line

Prerequisites→Core 1→Core 2→Elective→Elective→Capstone 1→Capstone 2→CFE · 3 days

With 30 months of practical experience at any point along the way.W33W16

WhenHow it ends
Jan 23, 2027Final Core 1 session begins: the last way into the program.W25
Sep 8–10, 2027The only CFE of 2027.W25QC11
Sep 26–28, 2028The final CFE.W25QC11
Dec 31, 2028The last day to complete the program.W13ON14 In the West, eligible candidates who have not finished must apply to transition by this date. In Ontario, CPA Ontario transitions eligible students who have not finished.W13ON14

02How the current program works

The roadmap from prerequisites to membership. Select a step for its content, its exam and how each region delivers it.

Prior experience3 to 12 months may be recognized
Practical experience: 30 months in totalin a pre-approved program or by experience verification, at any time within the time limit, including after the CFE
Step 2 of 8
Module 1

Core 1: financial accounting and reporting

  • Core 1 centres on financial accounting and reporting. Together the two core modules build breadth across the technical areas and draw on law, economics, finance, strategy, statistics and IT. A10W22
  • About eight weeks of online learning with weekly assignments, 15 to 20 hours of study a week, and a mandatory two-day workshop. A two-day orientation workshop precedes Core 1. W22W29
  • Ends with a four-hour, in-person exam of objective-format questions and short cases. CPA Canada sets the dates and marks every exam nationally. W28W29
  • Candidates who miss the workshop cannot write the exam. W22
OntarioModule fee $1,525 + HST. Exams are written at centres across Ontario. ON18ON20
QuebecNational Program: online modules with in-class workshops, exams at a centre in Montréal, and a coach for each group of 6 to 10. University students take equivalent courses instead. QC16QC17QC20
WestModule fee $1,630 + GST. Final session Jan 23 – Mar 24, 2027; last exam, rewrite only, Jun 30, 2027. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,910 + HST. A 20-week extended version was offered alongside the eight-week one. A10

All 8 steps

Step 1 · Before you start

Entry: a degree, 120 credit hours and 14 prerequisite courses

  • A degree and 120 credit hours of post-secondary education, plus 14 prerequisite courses: nine core and five non-core. W27W30
  • Grades: at least 60% in each core course, 50% in each non-core course, and a 65% average across the core courses. W27ON18ON19
  • Missing prerequisites can be taken at a post-secondary institution, through the profession’s own preparatory courses, or a mix of both. W27ON19
  • Preparatory courses are not part of the certification program itself; they exist to fill prerequisite gaps. W33
OntarioCPA Ontario runs its own preparatory courses (PREP). A four-year degree, or 120 credit hours, is required. The last PREP exam is December 2026. ON19ON18ON14
QuebecA recognized bachelor’s degree includes all the prerequisite courses for admission to CPA PEP. Then comes either a university graduate program (minimum average 2.8/4.3, set by each university) or the National Program delivered by the Order. QC23QC16QC18
WestCPAWSB preparatory courses cover all 14 prerequisites; at least one core course per competency area must be within 10 years. Applicants without a degree can use an eight-year “mature status” route. Courses end December 2027. W27W30
AtlanticCPA Atlantic preparatory courses cost $850 per core course and $655 per non-core course and run until December 2027. Applications to CPA PEP itself have closed. A11A10
Step 2 · Module 1

Core 1: financial accounting and reporting

  • Core 1 centres on financial accounting and reporting. Together the two core modules build breadth across the technical areas and draw on law, economics, finance, strategy, statistics and IT. A10W22
  • About eight weeks of online learning with weekly assignments, 15 to 20 hours of study a week, and a mandatory two-day workshop. A two-day orientation workshop precedes Core 1. W22W29
  • Ends with a four-hour, in-person exam of objective-format questions and short cases. CPA Canada sets the dates and marks every exam nationally. W28W29
  • Candidates who miss the workshop cannot write the exam. W22
OntarioModule fee $1,525 + HST. Exams are written at centres across Ontario. ON18ON20
QuebecNational Program: online modules with in-class workshops, exams at a centre in Montréal, and a coach for each group of 6 to 10. University students take equivalent courses instead. QC16QC17QC20
WestModule fee $1,630 + GST. Final session Jan 23 – Mar 24, 2027; last exam, rewrite only, Jun 30, 2027. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,910 + HST. A 20-week extended version was offered alongside the eight-week one. A10
Step 3 · Module 2

Core 2: management accounting, planning and control

  • Core 2 centres on management accounting, planning and control. A10
  • Same format as Core 1: about eight weeks online, a two-day workshop and a four-hour exam. W29W22W28
  • Core 1 must be completed before Core 2 unless the two are taken together on the fast-track pathway, which takes about 40 hours a week. W28W29
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Final Core 2 exam September 2027. ON18ON14
QuebecEach National Program module costs $1,747.62 with taxes. Last offering Jul 24 – Sep 17, 2027. QC19QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final session Jul 24 – Sep 22, 2027. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 4 · Modules 3 and 4

Two elective modules: the specialization choice

  • Candidates choose two of four: Assurance, Taxation, Finance and Performance Management. The focus is depth. W22
  • Both core modules must be complete before the electives. Each elective ends with its own four-hour exam. W29W28
  • Public accounting requires the Assurance and Taxation electives. W22ON21
  • The elective choice also shapes the CFE: Day 2 is written in one of four roles that mirror the electives. ON21W32
OntarioEach elective $1,450 + HST. Final elective exams March 2028. ON18ON14
QuebecGraduate-program students choose two of the four as university courses; the Assurance and Taxation courses are needed for the CPA auditor designation. QC16QC18
WestEach elective $1,470 + GST. Final session Jan 29 – Mar 29, 2028; all elective exams fall on the same day, so candidates are told to plan for one. W31W25
AtlanticEach elective $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 5 · Module 5

Capstone 1: the integrative team case

  • Teams work through one large business case, building strategic leadership, teamwork and communication skills. The same case is the basis of Day 1 of the CFE. W22W32
  • There is no exam. Candidates are evaluated on a group report and an oral presentation to a panel. W32QC17
  • Two electives must be passed before Capstone 1. W28
  • Each Capstone 1 case is used for two CFE sittings. W32
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Recommended immediately before the CFE: Capstone 1 from May for a September CFE. ON18ON17
QuebecAssessed on three components: individual contribution to teamwork, the group report and the oral presentation. Last offered spring 2028. QC17QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final offering May 27 – Jul 28, 2028, presentations Jul 21–27. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 6 · Module 6

Capstone 2: preparation for the Common Final Examination

  • Applies everything learned so far to complex, highly integrative practice cases. W22W32
  • No module exam. Candidates must complete a set number of practice cases to become eligible for the CFE. W32
  • Practice cases use the candidate’s declared elective role, the same role tested on Day 2 of the CFE. W32
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Recommended from July for a September CFE. ON18ON17
QuebecNo exam; once complete, the candidate can write the CFE. Last offered summer 2028. QC17QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final offering starts Aug 5, 2028. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 7 · National exam

The Common Final Examination (CFE)

  • A three-day, 13-hour examination: Day 1 four hours, Day 2 five hours, Day 3 four hours. First-time writers must attempt all three days in the same sitting. W21W32
  • Day 1 is based on the Capstone 1 case. Day 2 tests depth in one of four elective roles together with Financial Reporting or Management Accounting. Days 2 and 3 together test depth and breadth, and the three-day CFE requires breadth across all six technical competencies. W32ON21ON22W21ON22
  • Three attempts. Unlike module exams, the CFE cannot be deferred. QC17QC1W21
  • Only two sittings remain: Sep 8–10, 2027 and Sep 26–28, 2028. There are no May sittings. W25QC11
OntarioFee $2,050 + HST for all three days. Final CFE September 2028. ON18ON14
QuebecFee $1,997.12 with taxes. Written in French or English. QC19QC17
WestFee $2,070 + GST. First-attempt pass rate in 2025 was 69.8% (CPABC). W31BC1
AtlanticFee $1,940 + HST. A10
Step 8 · Finish

Membership: education, the CFE and practical experience

  • The certification program has three parts: CPA PEP, the CFE and 30 months of paid practical experience. W33BC1
  • Experience does not have to be finished before the CFE; it can be completed at any time within the program time limit. W16
  • A public accounting licence needs the Assurance and Taxation electives, the Assurance role on the CFE with depth in Assurance and Financial Reporting, and chargeable hours in audit or assurance. ON21
OntarioDeregistration deadlines: six years after starting CPA PEP unless the CFE has been attempted; seven years to finish experience; ten years after first registration. ON23
QuebecThe whole path must be completed within seven years of registering as a candidate. Practical experience is 24 months. QC16QC9
WestSix years for CPA PEP and seven years overall, with up to 24 months of approved leave. W23
AtlanticUp to six years for CPA PEP and the CFE. A10

Module boxes are pale; exams are dark. Core 1 and Core 2 subjects as described by CPA Atlantic.A10A10 Elective choice, exam length, Capstone assessment and CFE days as described by CPAWSB; the Quebec Order describes the CFE as a consecutive three-day exam.W22W29W32W32W32W32QC1 Unlike the new program, experience is not a gate before the final exam. Experience bar as described by CPAWSB; Quebec requires 24 months.W24W16QC9

03The current exams and the CFE

Four module exams, one team presentation and the three-day Common Final Examination: 29 hours of written exams in all (our sum: four 4-hour module exams and 13 CFE hours).W28W21 CPA Canada sets the exam dates and marks all exams.W28

The Common Final Examination, day by day

Block widths are proportional to writing time: 4, 5 and 4 hours.W21W32

Day 1 · 4 hoursThe Capstone 1 case

Builds on the business case the candidate’s team worked through in Capstone 1.W32ON22

Day 2 · 5 hoursDepth in one role

One case for everyone, with separate appendices for each of four roles: Assurance, Finance, Performance Management, Tax. Tests the elective area plus Financial Reporting or Management Accounting.ON21

Day 3 · 4 hoursWith Day 2: depth and breadth

CPAWSB says Days 2 and 3 test the depth and breadth of candidates’ competency development. CPA Ontario says the three-day CFE requires breadth across all six technical competencies.W21ON22

How long each exam is

Hours of writing time.W28W29W21 Candidates choose two of the four electives; Day 2 tests depth in the declared elective role, and Days 2 and 3 together test depth and breadth.W22W32W21

Four module exams (16 hours) plus the CFE (13 hours) make 29 hours.W29W32 The new program has 16 or 18, depending on the version of the CPA Core exam: 5 hours for Foundational Development, 3 or 5 for CPA Core, 5 for CPA Leadership and 3 for Professional Readiness.N1 Both totals are our sums.

Rules that apply

  • Module exams combine objective-format questions and short cases and are written in person.W28QC17
  • Capstone 1 is assessed by a team report and oral presentation, not an exam; Capstone 2 has no exam.W32QC17
  • Three attempts at each exam. In Quebec a second failure means retaking the module, and a third means expulsion from the program.QC17
  • First-time CFE writers must attempt all three days in one sitting, and the CFE cannot be deferred.W21
  • The Day 2 role is declared in advance and can be any of the four, though candidates are advised to pick one matching an elective they completed.ON21W32
  • A module exam can be deferred once the module work is complete, but the next sitting must then be attempted.QC17
  • CPA Canada publishes annual pass rates for first-time writers. CPABC reports 69.8% for the 2025 CFE.QC17BC1
Public accounting under the current program. Complete the Tax and Assurance electives, select the Assurance role on Day 2, demonstrate depth in Assurance and Financial Reporting on the CFE, and meet the chargeable-hour experience requirements.ON21

Example pathways

Four generic routes, drawn to the same four-year scale. They are illustrations built from the published rules, not any one university’s schedule. Months are typical, and the experience bar assumes 30 months starting when full-time work begins.

Graduate diploma in the summer, then a firm

The Ontario diploma design: 20 of the 42 Ontario rows on CPA Canada’s list cover only Core 1, Core 2 and two electives, the largest group (our count). The two diplomas cited here run 13 weeks. The timeline assumes full-time work starts in September; the graduate then takes Capstone 1 from May and Capstone 2 from July in CPA PEP, as CPA Ontario recommends for a September CFE, and writes the CFE that September. N4U4U7ON17

Time off around Capstone 2 and the CFE is arranged with the employer; CPAWSB notes the program assumes only the few days between Capstone 2 and the CFE. One university says Capstone 1, Capstone 2 and the CFE can be completed in five months. W32U16

Master’s program covering all six modules

Some master’s programs include both Capstones, so their graduates go straight to the CFE. In the West the two accredited master’s programs run over two summers, with work in between; Waterloo’s MAcc took eight months. N4U34X1U2

CPA PEP part time while working

The route with no university program: one module per session, which most candidates take while working full time. The most common time to finish the six modules is 16 to 24 months. W29

University graduate program in Quebec

A DESS replaces all six modules; HEC’s current program is a 16-month cohort. Students fit a work term inside the program and must also pass the CFE, which the Order’s calendar lists for September. Quebec requires 24 months of experience. N4QC21QC18QC11QC9

Delivered by a universityDelivered by the CPA bodyPaid work counting as experienceNational exam

Illustrations only. Module coverage and program lengths are from the cited sources. The CFE is a three-day examination, and the work bars run for the required practical experience: 30 months, or 24 in Quebec. W21W24QC9 The month-by-month layout and the experience end dates are our arithmetic.

07Experience in the current program

Thirty months of paid, relevant experience, tracked in the Practical Experience Reporting Tool (PERT), through one of two routes. It is independent of the exam sequence.W24ON25W16

30 months of practical experience, including up to five months away from workW24W16

Practical experience
30 months, developing breadth and depth of technical competencies and enabling competenciesW24W24

Pre-approved program route

  • A training position approved in advance and designed to meet the requirements within 30 months.W24ON25
  • The employer matches the candidate with a CPA mentor; less documentation is required.W24
  • Offered by public accounting firms, government and corporate employers.A13

Experience verification route

  • The candidate chooses the employer and role, and files detailed experience reports that the profession reviews.W24
  • The candidate finds their own CPA mentor.W24A13
  • In Ontario the position is pre-assessed before reporting can begin.ON25
  • Candidates meet their CPA mentor at least twice a year.W24A13
  • Three to 12 months of prior experience may be recognized toward the 30 months.W24
  • Quebec is different: 24 months, with at most 8 earned before registering with the Order and at least 16 after, and a report every six months.QC9QC1
  • CPA Ontario gives December 2028 as the final date to complete experience requirements in PERT. Eligible candidates can transition their experience to the new program; in the West this is by application.ON6W13

09The new program at a glance

The new program consists of the Foundational Development module and three professional modules, with a Knowledge Assessment at entry for learners who are not exempt. The CPA profession strives for national consistency, but provincial regulations and bylaws take precedence over national requirements, so learners must refer to the regulations of their own provincial body.W11N2

4modules, taken in orderW5
4exams: one module exam and a three-part Professional Final ExamW6
16hof exams on the Common path, 18 h on the Licensure pathN1
24moof experience, finished before the last moduleON5W9ON1
3× a yearexam sittings: January, May, SeptemberA3ON4
7yrmaximum to finish in Ontario and the West; also the cap after transition in Quebec and AtlanticON13W11QC1A5

What to know first

  • The last exam comes after the experience. A learner cannot start the final module, CPA Professional Readiness, until all 24 months of experience are complete.ON1W5QC2A1
  • The three-day CFE is replaced by three Professional Final Exams, each written right after its module.W16QC1
  • CPA Core has two pathways: Common or Licensure. Those seeking a public accounting licence must pass the Licensure version.N2ON1
  • Entry no longer depends on fixed prerequisite courses. Applicants show accounting knowledge through coursework or a new Knowledge Assessment.W16N1
  • The current program runs out on Dec 31, 2028. The final CFE is September 2028.ON6W14A1

Four dates define the changeover

WhenWhat happens
Jan 2027CPA Ontario’s launch date for the new program. Registration for the Quebec Order’s program begins; in the West it opens in early 2027. The 24-month transition period opens (January 2027 to December 2028).ON1W1QC1ON6
May 2027First new-program modules start (West and Atlantic May 15, Ontario online May 31, Quebec Order program in May).W7A2ON2QC1
Sep 15–16, 2027First new-program exams, on the same dates in every region.ON4QC4W7
Dec 31, 2028Transition window closes and CPA PEP ends.W13ON6

CPA Ontario says the program “will launch in January 2027” and CPABC says it “launches in May 2027”. CPAWSB’s timeline shows both steps: learners can begin to transition in January 2027 and the first new modules are offered in May 2027.ON1BC1W1

Select a step to see what it involves, how it is examined, and how each region delivers it. The walkthrough plays the steps in order.

Ontario14 weeks, delivered by accredited universities, not CPA Ontario: online through Executive Education at Rotman, Waterloo or Ivey (self-paced, minimum 15 hours a week), or in-person in a graduate program. First online offering May 31, 2027. Accredited in-person programs may deliver their own equivalent of the module exam. ON2ON13

AtlanticSame design and dates as the West: first start May 15, 2027, registration from January 2027. The schedule lists the two-day orientation workshop as online. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. A2

All 7 steps

Step 1 · Before you start

Entry: degree, credits, and proof of accounting knowledge

  • A degree (or equivalent), at least 120 credit hours, a minimum GPA set by the region, and evidence of good character. ON9W2A2
  • Accounting and business knowledge is shown one of two ways: recognized post-secondary coursework, or passing the Knowledge Assessment. N2ON9W3
  • Knowledge Assessment: 150 objective-format questions in 5 hours. Part A is 3 hours (90 questions across eight topic areas), Part B is 2 hours (60 questions, half Financial Reporting and half Management Decision-Making). No reference materials. To pass you need sufficiency on Financial Reporting, on Management Decision-Making, and overall. N1
  • Offered three times a year. First sitting: March 23, 2027. ON4W7W4
OntarioMinimum 70% GPA across the 120 credit hours. Knowledge is shown by the 15 CPA Qualifying Courses (7 named + 8 other business courses) or the Knowledge Assessment, completed within three years before enrolling in Foundational Development. Up to three Knowledge Assessment attempts. Non-degree route: eight years of relevant experience. ON9ON10ON11ON12
QuebecA bachelor’s degree recognized by the Order (or the equivalence process), obtained within the five years before applying. No minimum average for the program delivered by the Order; universities set their own. QC1
WestMinimum 65% GPA on the most recent 60 credit hours. Knowledge is 45 credit hours (21 in required topics + 24 other) or the Knowledge Assessment; currency window is five years. Non-degree applicants can use an eight-year “advanced experience” pathway. W2W11
AtlanticMinimum 65% GPA. Same 45-credit-hour rule (21 + 24) with one course inside five years, or the Knowledge Assessment (result valid five years). A2A6A3
Step 2 · Module 1

Module 1: Foundational Development

  • Develops the Specific, Foundational and Sub-Foundational Competencies and begins the CPA Advanced Professional Competencies. Experience reporting can begin when this module starts. N2W5
  • You must pass the module’s own assessments before you can sit its exam. W5ON2
  • Foundational Development Exam: 5 hours. 50 objective-format questions (33%) plus 4 to 8 testlets (67%). Pass requires sufficiency on Financial Reporting and Management Decision-Making combined, and overall. Handbooks, Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act available. Non-disclosed. N1
  • This is the only module exam that is not part of the three-part Professional Final Exam. W6W16
Ontario14 weeks, delivered by accredited universities, not CPA Ontario: online through Executive Education at Rotman, Waterloo or Ivey (self-paced, minimum 15 hours a week), or in-person in a graduate program. First online offering May 31, 2027. Accredited in-person programs may deliver their own equivalent of the module exam. ON2ON13
Quebec16 weeks + 2 weeks of exam preparation, online in the Order’s program; or equivalent university courses. Order modules begin May 2027. The exam is run by the universities for graduate-program candidates and by the Order for its own candidates. QC3QC1
WestOnline, weekly submissions, with a two-day in-person orientation workshop. Standard track (about 20 h/week) or flexible track (about 10 h/week). First start May 15, 2027; registration opens Feb 1, 2027. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. W5W7W8
AtlanticSame design and dates as the West: first start May 15, 2027, registration from January 2027. The schedule lists the two-day orientation workshop as online. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. A2
Step 3 · Module 2

Module 2: CPA Core, in a Common or a Licensure version

  • CPA Core – Common builds financial reporting, assurance and trust, big data and analytics, and tax. CPA Core – Licensure contains all of Common plus more depth, and is required for anyone who wants a public accounting licence. N2W5ON1
  • Professional Final Exam 1, Common: two to three cases of 60 to 120 minutes each, 3 hours in total. N1
  • Professional Final Exam 1, Licensure: Part A is the same cases as the Common exam (3 hours); Part B is one 2-hour licensure case. Passing needs overall sufficiency and “readiness for licensure” on Part B. N1
  • A candidate who passes only Part A still progresses in the program; a separate licensure exam can be written after certification. N1
OntarioCommon 8 weeks (first online offering Jul 12, 2027); Licensure 14 weeks (first online offering May 31, 2027). ON2
QuebecThe licensure version is called “Core – Common + Public accountancy” and leads to the CPA auditor designation. Common 8 weeks + 2; Common + Public accountancy 14 weeks + 2. QC3QC1
WestLicensure first starts May 29, 2027, Common Jul 10, 2027; both lead to the Sep 16, 2027 exam. Either module $1,600; exam $1,350. W7W8
AtlanticSame start dates as the West (May 29 and Jul 10, 2027). Either module $1,600; exam $1,350. A2
Step 4 · Module 3

Module 3: CPA Leadership

  • Applies the decision process to real-world challenges that integrate every topic area; the focus is critical thinking and the CPA Ethical Mindset. N2
  • Professional Final Exam 2: one 5-hour comprehensive case of moderate complexity, with limited direction and designed to be time-pressured. This is the only disclosed exam in the program. N1
  • Heaviest content areas on the exam: Strategy, Risk Management and Innovation (20–35%), Ethical Decision-Making and Governance (15–30%), Management Decision-Making (15–30%). N1
Ontario10 weeks; first online offering Jun 28, 2027. Exam 1 may be written before or after this module. ON2ON13
Quebec10 weeks + 2 weeks of exam preparation, online. Each exam must be passed before moving to the next module. QC3QC2
WestFirst start Jun 26, 2027. Learners may take Leadership before writing Exam 1, but on a first attempt Exam 1 must be written before or together with Exam 2. Module $2,000; exam $1,400. W7W11W8
AtlanticFirst start Jun 26, 2027. Module $2,000; exam $1,400. A2
Step 5 · Checkpoint

Checkpoint: experience must be finished before the last module

  • Every region requires all experience requirements to be met before a learner can register for CPA Professional Readiness. This is the main structural change from the current program. ON1W5A1QC2
  • 24 months of qualifying experience, net of leaves: up to 8 months of Foundational experience and at least 16 months of Professional experience. ON5W9A1QC6
  • In Ontario and the West, Professional experience needs a CPA mentor and an experience (work) plan approved by the provincial body before it starts to count. In Quebec a CPA mentor must accompany the candidate and approve the work plan, which the Order must then approve. ON5W11QC6QC1
OntarioFoundational experience can date from up to five years before Foundational Development; all 24 months can be Professional if the role is already at that level. Full-time is 35 hours a week. ON5ON12
QuebecExperience must be completed and recognized by the Order. Full-time is at least 32 hours a week; the Order checks only a work plan at the start and a report at the end. QC2QC6
WestExams 1 and 2 must also be passed. Full-time equivalent is 35 hours a week. Organizations can hold “pre-reviewed” experience plans. W11
AtlanticExams 1 and 2 and all practical experience must be complete before the module. CPA ASB approves the work plan. A1A7
Step 6 · Module 4

Module 4: CPA Professional Readiness

  • Self-study plus a five-day, in-person, case-based experience covering the code of conduct, teamwork, and emerging global, social and technological issues. W5ON1N2
  • Professional Final Exam 3: one 2-hour professional-judgment case and one 1-hour ethical decision-making case. Each case is marked holistically and both must be passed. Not designed to be time-pressured. N1
  • After passing Exam 3 the learner applies for membership in their province. W5A1
OntarioDelivered by CPA Ontario itself, five days in person. The first module “takes place in winter 2028”; first Exam 3 is Jan 20, 2028. No exemptions from this module. ON2ON4ON13
QuebecDelivered only by the Order, for both pathways: 5 days in person plus 2 weeks of online preparation. QC3QC5
WestFirst offering starts Dec 11, 2027 with the in-person workshop Dec 13–17, 2027; Exam 3 on Jan 20, 2028. Module $1,800; exam $1,400. W7W8
AtlanticSame first offering: starts Dec 11, 2027, workshop Dec 13–17, 2027. Module $1,800; exam $1,400. A2
Step 7 · Finish

Membership

  • The designation and its legal recognition do not change; graduates of the new program receive the same CPA designation. QC1
  • Public accounting licensure is applied for after membership and requires the Licensure version of CPA Core and Exam 1 plus the licensure experience. W11ON1
OntarioLicensure pathway: all 24 months in an External Audit Training Office, with at least 2,500 chargeable hours including 1,250 in assurance (625 audit). ON15ON5
QuebecCPA auditor: 24 months at an audit firm including 1,250 assurance hours, 625 of them auditing general-purpose financial statements. QC1
WestAudit: 1,250 chargeable assurance hours, at least 625 in audit. Review: 1,250, at least 625 in audit or review. Compilation: 625. W11
AtlanticLicensure experience needs a Licensed Public Accountant as mentor and an organization registered for public accounting with the provincial body; applicable chargeable hours are required to meet licensure requirements. A7

11The new exams

The exams are national and will be consistent across the country, each with its own blueprint. The Board of Examiners sets the passing standard for each exam, and results are determined on a national basis regardless of where learners live or the language in which they write.N1A3BC2

How long each exam is

Hours of writing time. Exams with two parts are shown split. The time for each part is controlled in the Knowledge Assessment and the CPA Core – Licensure exam; in the Professional Readiness exam, candidates manage the time between the two cases themselves.N1

Part A: 2–3 cases · Part B: one 2-hour case

Rules that apply to every exam

  • A module must be passed before its exam can be written.W5ON2
  • Three attempts per module and per exam in Ontario, the West and Atlantic; Quebec states three attempts at each part of the Professional Final Exam. An exam must be attempted within one year of completing its module in the West and Quebec, and successfully completed within one year in Ontario; if not, an attempt is counted.ON13W11QC1A3
  • All exams are written in person, on computer, at an exam centre.ON12QC1
  • Reference material provided: the CPA Canada Handbooks, the Income Tax Act and the Excise Tax Act. The Knowledge Assessment has none.N1
  • Testable standards and tax law reset once a year: exams from May 1 to the following April 30 use what was effective on January 1 of that year.N1
  • Only the CPA Leadership exam is disclosed after the sitting; the others are non-disclosed.N1
  • Two Specific Competencies are assessed inside the modules and not on any exam: SC4 (how standards and laws are developed and why they matter) and SC6 (the impact of technological innovation and automation).N1N3
  • Up to 10% of objective questions on the Knowledge Assessment and the Foundational Development Exam are unscored pre-test items.N1

12The new program, region by region

This guide compares four bodies (our count). CPAWSB’s policies name CPA Ontario, CPA Quebec and the CPA Atlantic School of Business among the other bodies.W11 They say CPAWSB administers the program for learners in the Western Region.W11 Start with what is distinctive about each, then use the table to compare them module by module.

Who covers where

Select a province or territory to jump to its regional body.

OntarioQuebecWest (CPAWSB)Atlantic (CPA ASB)

Western Region membership from the CPAWSB policies; Atlantic Region from the CPA Atlantic transition policy and its costs and fees page.W11A5A11 In Ontario, students register with CPA Ontario; in Quebec, the program delivered by the Order is one of two pathways to become a CPA.ON9QC2

How to read differences. The profession “strives for national consistency; however, provincial regulations and bylaws take precedence over national requirements”. Employers and learners in more than one province are told to check each body’s rules.W11

Ontario

CPA Ontario
  • Universities teach the first three modules and set their fees. Online through Rotman, Waterloo or Ivey Executive Education, or in person in an accredited graduate program. ON2ON12
  • 70% GPA across the required 120 credit hours; entry-level knowledge (the final qualifying course, or the Knowledge Assessment) must be completed within three years before enrolling in Foundational Development. ON9
  • Transition is automatic. CPA Ontario moves students across on fixed cut-off dates from July 15, 2027; registration by Dec 31, 2026 is needed to stay on the current CFE route. ON14ON6
  • Regulations in effect, fees not yet shared. Regulations 9-3 and 9-4 took effect Nov 1, 2026; CPA Ontario says fees for the examinations and modules “will be shared when available”. ON13ON14ON4

Quebec

Ordre des CPA du Québec
  • Two pathways: the Order’s online program or a graduate program at one of 11 universities; both end with the Order’s Professional Readiness module. QC2QC5
  • No minimum average for the Order’s program; the degree must be recent (five years). QC1
  • Strictly sequential: pass each exam before the next module. The Module 1 exam is run by the universities for their own students. QC2QC1
  • Practical experience was already 24 months in Quebec; what changes is the Foundational / Professional split and lighter monitoring. QC9QC6

West and the territories

CPAWSB with CPABC, CPA Alberta, CPA Saskatchewan, CPA Manitoba, CPA Yukon, CPA NWT/Nunavut
  • Most complete rulebook so far: full fee schedule, dated module and exam calendar to September 2028, and published policies. W8W7W11
  • Standard or flexible pace (about 20 or 10 hours a week), with a two-day in-person orientation. W5W11
  • 65% GPA on the last 60 credits; eight-year experience route for applicants without a degree. W11
  • Up to two extra years on transition. One set of policies covers all four provinces and the territories. W12W11

Atlantic and Bermuda

CPA Atlantic School of Business with CPA NS, NB, NL, PEI and Bermuda
  • Same calendar and module fees as the West; first modules May 15, 2027, registration from January 2027. A2
  • Only region with an official total: about $16,800 + HST for the program over 2.5 years, including a $500 one-time registration fee. A2
  • The school approves work plans: a Professional work plan must be approved by the mentor and CPA ASB, and CPA ASB reviews experience before a transition. Under the transition policy, the transition application itself is approved by the relevant Atlantic provincial body. A7A4
  • Up to three extra years on transition; preparatory course registration closes Oct 20, 2027. A3A1

13Universities in the new program

In Ontario, accredited post-secondary institutions deliver every module except Professional Readiness, and only CPA Ontario delivers the Professional Final Exams. In Quebec there is a university pathway and an Order pathway; the Professional Final Exams and the Professional Readiness module are offered by the Order only. In the West two master’s programs are accredited, and accredited programs exclude the Professional Final Exams. As of Nov 18, 2026, CPA Atlantic’s program page named no accredited university program.ON13QC1QC3W20W11A2

Example pathways

Generic routes on the same four-year scale as the current-program examples, so the two can be compared. They are illustrations built from the published rules and exam calendar (sittings each September, January and May), not any one university’s schedule. The experience bar assumes 24 months from the start of full-time work.

In-person graduate program in the summer, then a firm

The Ontario diploma model. A 12 or 13-week accredited diploma satisfies Foundational Development, CPA Core and CPA Leadership. Its graduates are exempt from CPA Ontario’s Foundational Development exam (the university may be approved to deliver its own) and can write Exams 1 and 2 as early as September of the same year. The timeline then shows full-time work, and the five-day Professional Readiness module once the minimum 24 months of work experience are complete. ON13U4U8ON1

If up to eight months of earlier co-op counts as Foundational experience, the 24 months finish sooner and Exam 3 moves up one or two sittings. Not every program follows this shape: Guelph’s master’s places Exam 1 in September and Exam 2 in January. ON5U1U26

Modules part time while working

The route with no graduate program: through the regional school in the West and Atlantic, online through a partner university in Ontario, or through the Order in Quebec. Each module is followed by its exam. W7A2ON2QC2

Dates follow the western regular-track calendar. In Ontario the three modules on this route are delivered online by a university rather than by the CPA body. W7ON2 The work bar is our arithmetic: 24 months of full-time qualifying experience counted from the start of Foundational Development. Under the western policies, Professional experience can accumulate once the learner is enrolled in that module, has a mentor and has an approved experience plan. W9W11

University graduate program in Quebec

HEC Montréal’s published sequence: courses in summer and fall, Exam 1 in January, a winter work term, CPA Leadership the next summer and Exam 2 in September. Professional Readiness and Exam 3 follow with the Order once the practical experience, which lasts a minimum of 24 months, is complete. QC13QC3QC6

Master’s over two summers (West)

The University of Saskatchewan’s published pathway: year 1 courses then Exam 1, year 2 courses then Exam 2, work in between, and Professional Readiness with Exam 3 at the end. CPAWSB’s FAQ says students in the two accredited programs will receive advanced placement and that more information “will be available soon”. U34U35W18 The two work bars add up to the minimum of 24 months of full-time qualifying experience on CPAWSB’s experience page (our arithmetic). W9

Delivered by a universityDelivered by the CPA bodyPaid work counting as experienceNational exam

Illustrations only. Exam sittings follow the published September, January and May pattern. The end of each work bar, and the placing of Professional Readiness at the first offering after the 24 months are complete, are our arithmetic. W7ON4A3W18

15Experience in the new program

The experience requirement drops to 24 months, splits into two levels, and moves ahead of the final module. One model replaces the two current routes.W16ON5

24 months of qualifying experience, net of leaves

Foundational
up to 8 months
Professional
at least 16 months
  • Foundational experience can be entry-level but must involve decisions and judgment; it cannot be clerical. It may come from before the program starts.W9W11
  • Professional experience counts once the learner is enrolled in Foundational Development, has a CPA mentor, and has submitted an experience plan that the provincial body approves.W11ON5
  • All 24 months can be Professional if the role is already at that level.ON5QC6
  • Time off, including vacation and leaves, does not count toward the 24 months.A1W16
  • Learners must reach the top proficiency level in Financial Reporting or Management Accounting.W9W11
  • Ontario’s task statements: three Foundational (F1–F3); Professional in Financial Reporting (FR1–FR4) or Management Accounting (MA1–MA4), plus Professional Skepticism, Ethical Decision Making and Communication (DC1–DC3). Assurance & Trust (AT1) is added for licensure.ON5
  • Training areas named by Ontario and Quebec: Financial Reporting, Management Accounting, Assurance & Trust, Taxation, Finance, Strategy & Governance, Non-Financial Reporting, Data. The Western policy lists ten, adding Value Creation and Ethical Decision-Making and Governance.ON5QC6W11

Eligibility checklist used in the West and AtlanticW12A4

  • Program time limit ends after Dec 31, 2028.W12A4
  • Active status and good standing with the provincial body at the time of transition.W12A4
  • Re-enrolment (annual renewal in Atlantic) completed for the current academic year, and no outstanding fees.W12W12A4A4
  • Experience reporting in PERT up to date, with reports reviewed and approved.W12W15A4
  • Good character requirements met; no outstanding penalties or unresolved disciplinary matters.W12W12A4A4
  • In full compliance with the CPA PEP Training Contract (West) or the required candidate training contracts (Atlantic).W12A4

In the new program, transitioned candidates get three attempts per module and exam regardless of earlier attempts, and cannot return to CPA PEP. In the West they do not pay fees twice for the same requirement.W12W15A3A4

Practical experience. In the West, candidates with less than 6 months approved by Jan 1, 2027 are steered to transition; with more than 12 months on a pre-approved route they are advised to stay. In Ontario, 8 or more months with three sub-competencies at Level 1 in PERT earns credit for the full eight months of Foundational experience.W15ON8ON14

19Planning notes for program managers

These points are our reading of what the official rules mean in practice. Each one rests on the cited rule; none is a statement by a CPA body.

Plan the finish date around experience, not coursework. On CPAWSB’s schedule the first Foundational Development offering starts on May 15, 2027 and a CPA Leadership exam falls on May 17, 2028; our reading is that the three education modules can be finished in about a year.W7W7 In the West, Professional experience can be accumulated only once the learner is enrolled in Foundational Development, has a mentor and has submitted an experience plan, and at least 16 months are required.W11W11 By our arithmetic, a learner who starts in May 2027 reaches 16 months in mid-September 2028 at the earliest, after CPAWSB’s Professional Readiness offering of Aug 19, 2028 has started; experience must be met before that module.W7W16 As of Nov 18, 2026 CPAWSB’s schedule showed no dates in 2029.W7 CPA Ontario’s schedule lists an Exam 3 sitting on Jan 18, 2029; that date is Ontario’s, not CPAWSB’s.ON4
Put the mentor and the experience plan in place at day one. In the West, Professional experience counts no earlier than the date the plan is submitted, and none is recognized while a learner has no CPA mentor.W11W11 Our reading: late paperwork delays the final module, because experience must be met before Professional Readiness.W16
Check mentor capacity early. In Ontario and the West, the CPA mentor must work in the same organization as the learner.ON5W11 Quebec allows a CPA from the candidate’s network when the employer has none (not for public accountancy); British Columbia learners with no CPA mentor at their workplace are told to contact CPABC.QC6W11
Plan around the three exam windows each year. Exams are offered in January, May and September, and each module offering on CPAWSB’s schedule ends with one of those exam dates.A3W7 A missed window costs about four months (our arithmetic from those months). In the West an exam not attempted within one year of its module uses up one of the three attempts; in Ontario an attempt is counted if the exam is not successfully completed within that year.W11ON13
Budget time away for in-person parts. All exams are in person, Professional Readiness is five days in person, and the West adds a two-day in-person orientation at Module 1.ON2QC1W5
Make the licensure decision before CPA Core. In Ontario the Licensure version runs 14 weeks against 8 for Common. Its exam is five hours against three, and in the West licensure requires 24 months of experience in a registered, licensed CPA firm. A candidate who writes the Licensure exam and passes only Part A can continue in the program and will have a later chance, after certification, to write a separate exam for licensure.ON2N1W11
Sort current candidates now. Check three things for each case: whether the time limit runs past Dec 31, 2028, what has been completed in CPA PEP, and the experience recognized to date.W12W12 In the West and Atlantic a candidate must apply; in Ontario, CPA Ontario moves students on set dates, starting Jul 15, 2027 for those who have completed the Core 1 prerequisites but have not passed Core 1.W15A4ON14
Multi-province employers must check each provincial body’s rules. Provincial regulations and bylaws take precedence over national requirements, and organizations operating in several jurisdictions must refer to the regulations of each one. A learner must stay registered with the body where they live.W11 In the West, a transfer to another body is possible only after the Foundational Development Exam is passed.W11

20Side by side: how the new program differs from the current one

The comparison below uses CPAWSB’s official program comparison and the Order’s comparison chart. The current program is CPA PEP, the Common Final Examination and the practical experience requirement.W16QC9W12

DimensionCurrent program (to Dec 31, 2028)New CPA Professional Program (from 2027)
Academic entryDegree, 120 credit hours, 14 prerequisite courses taken within 10 years, 65% average on the prerequisites. W16Degree, 120 credit hours, 45 credit hours of accounting and business coursework or the Knowledge Assessment, and a regional GPA rule. W16
EducationSix CPA PEP modules: Core 1, Core 2, two electives, Capstone 1, Capstone 2, each built on eight weeks of online learning. W16W22Four modules: Foundational Development, CPA Core, CPA Leadership, CPA Professional Readiness. W16
SpecializationTwo electives chosen from Assurance, Taxation, Finance and Performance Management. QC9One choice: CPA Core – Common or CPA Core – Licensure. N2
Module examsAfter Core 1, Core 2 and each elective. W16One module exam, after Foundational Development. W16
Certification examThe three-day Common Final Examination after the final module: 4, 5 and 4 hours (13 hours, our sum). W16W21Three Professional Final Exams, each written after its module: 3 or 5 hours, 5 hours and 3 hours (11 or 13 hours, our sum). No consecutive three-day exam. W16N1QC1
Experience length30 months, inclusive of up to five months away from work (Quebec: 24 months). W16QC924 months, excluding time away from work. W16
Experience routesPre-approved program or experience verification, reported in PERT, with mentor meetings at least twice a year. W16W24One model: every learner submits an experience plan in advance; Foundational (up to 8 months) and Professional (at least 16 months) experience. W16ON5BC3
Experience before the program3 to 12 months of prior experience may be recognized. W24Up to 8 months, recognized as Foundational experience. W11ON5
Timing of experienceCan be completed at any time within the program time limit, including after the CFE. W16Must be complete before the last module and the last exam. W16ON1
Public accountingAssurance and Taxation electives. QC9CPA Core – Licensure and the Licensure version of Final Exam 1. ON1W11
Time limitSix years for CPA PEP and seven years overall, including experience. W23BC1Seven years for everything, in every region. ON13W11QC12A5
AttemptsThree attempts at the CFE in Quebec, where failing the third means expulsion under the Order’s current policy. Ontario’s transition regulation also refers to a third CFE attempt. QC1ON14Three attempts per module and per exam; transitioning candidates start with a fresh three. ON13W11QC1A3
Who sets the examsResults determined on a national basis: a CPABC article says the new program’s approach “follows the same model used for CPA PEP and the CFE”. BC2Unchanged in principle: the Board of Examiners oversees national exams and results are determined on a national basis. BC2N1
Typical figuresAbout 2.5 years; about $14,500; 69.8% first-attempt CFE pass rate in 2025 (CPABC). BC1Atlantic estimate about $16,800 + HST over 2.5 years. No pass rates exist yet. A2
Current path

Prerequisites → Core 1 → Core 2 → Elective → Elective → Capstone 1 → Capstone 2 → three-day CFE; 30 months of experience at any point within the time limit.W16BC1

New path

Knowledge shown → Foundational Development + exam → CPA Core + Exam 1 → CPA Leadership + Exam 2 → 24 months of experience complete → Professional Readiness + Exam 3.W16N2

Quebec’s current program already requires 24 months of practical experience, so the length does not change there; its structure and monitoring do.QC9

21Open items and inconsistencies

Things the official sources had not yet published or state differently from one page to another. Check these before relying on them.

Who approves a transition in Atlantic Canada. CPA Atlantic’s transition policy says a transition is not confirmed until approved by the Atlantic provincial body. Its transition FAQ says transition is confirmed only after the CPA Atlantic School of Business reviews and approves it. The two pages name different approvers. A4A3
“Launch” means different things. CPA Ontario says the program launches in January 2027; CPABC says May 2027. CPAWSB’s key dates put the start of the transition period at January 1, 2027, the first new-program modules in May 2027 and the first Professional Final Exams in September 2027. ON1BC1W1W13
Ontario prices and enrolment. As of Nov 18, 2026 CPA Ontario’s examination schedule page said enrolment details and fees for the examinations and modules “will be shared when available”. Its page on online and in-person study showed no tuition, said more details about enrolment “will be shared in late 2026”, and gave only “winter 2028” for the first Professional Readiness module. ON4ON2
Accreditation lists not final. Ontario’s university approval process was “anticipated to be completed in the fall”; Quebec’s lists were “subject to accreditation” in fall 2026, and for four Université du Québec campuses (our count) the page read “List will be available soon”. ON2QC5
Quebec fees, rules and the Knowledge Assessment. As of Nov 18, 2026 the Order’s “Costs, policies and rules” page read “Coming soon”; its page on the program it delivers gave module durations “for information purposes only”; and neither of those pages nor the new-program overview page mentioned a Knowledge Assessment. QC8QC2QC1
Western policies are a draft. The Education and Experience Policies are marked “Draft published May 2026”. The sections on regional transfers, advanced placement for accredited learners and international learners read “To come”, and the Learner Guide is due in early 2027. W11
Summary pages lag the schedules. CPAWSB’s key-date lists give months (“July 2028” for the last Capstone 2) while its schedule gives Aug 5, 2028; one page says final Core 1 registration closes in early November 2026 while the schedule shows Nov 23. CPA Atlantic’s overview mentions a Core 1 offering in May 2027 where the schedule shows an exam rewrite only. Use the dated schedules. W13W15W25A1
Atlantic details that differ between pages. The program description mentions a two-day in-person orientation, but the schedule lists the May 15–16, 2027 workshop as online. The new-program page says CPA ASB handles education delivery for CPA Nova Scotia, CPA New Brunswick, CPA Newfoundland and Labrador and CPA Bermuda, without naming Prince Edward Island; the Costs and Fees page names CPA Prince Edward Island as well, and the transition policy and the course lists also cover the province. A2A11A5A6
Sample exams may be revised. Sample cases “have not undergone the full range of processes and quality assurance checks”; corrected versions and full Knowledge Assessment and Foundational Development sample exams are due in early 2027. ON3W6
Western accredited master’s programs. CPAWSB says the University of Alberta MAcc and the University of Saskatchewan MPAcc will continue with advanced placement, but its policy section on accredited learners still reads “To come”. The University of Alberta says it “will not proceed with a new Master of Accounting intake in Spring 2027”. Saskatchewan’s brochure says students are exempt from the Foundational Development module and exam; no CPAWSB document confirms this or says which version of Exam 1 applies. W18W11X1U35 includes a non-CPA source
Who examines Ontario graduate-program students at the first stage. Regulation 9-3 exempts in-person graduates from the Foundational Development exam and lets an accredited university deliver an equivalent. University pages describe this differently: some say the exam is bypassed, Waterloo’s MAcc says students “write the Foundational Development examination”, and Queen’s says the assessment is administered by the school. Pages also differ on whether a program delivers CPA Core Common, Licensure or both. ON13U4U8U1U18 includes a non-CPA source
Ontario accreditation not confirmed school by school. CPA Ontario lists 17 institutions that applied for in-person accreditation but had not published approvals. University pages range from “under review” (Western DAN, York LA&PS) to “accredited” or “has received accreditation approval” (Ivey, Laurier, Guelph, Schulich). Toronto Metropolitan’s diploma takes its final intake in winter 2027 with no replacement page found; Ottawa and Lakehead show no redesigned program; Brock’s site could not be read; Toronto Mississauga’s MMPA is paused. ON2U6U15U13U25U12 includes a non-CPA source
Quebec and Atlantic university details. As of Nov 18, 2026 the Order’s page read “List will be available soon” for UQTR, UQAT, UQAC and UQAR, and all Quebec lists remain subject to accreditation. In Atlantic Canada, CPA Canada’s list (a 2023 Internet Archive copy) shows one accredited program, Saint Mary’s MBA-CPA Stream, which the university’s 2024–2025 calendar describes as accredited. On the same date CPA Atlantic’s new-program overview and program pages did not mention an accredited university program. QC5QC22N4U36A1A2 includes a non-CPA source
The national list of accredited programs is a 2023 snapshot. CPA Canada’s list of which CPA PEP modules each university program covers could only be read as a September 2023 copy from the Internet Archive. Programs have changed since (for example, Toronto Metropolitan was still listed as Ryerson). CPAWSB’s CFE page also lists Capstone 2 as a separate requirement, while the list shows the western master’s programs covering it. N4W21

23Reading list: documents saved with this guide

Official documents worth reading in full, saved in the references/ folder next to this file.

01 · National core documents

  • Exam Guide16 pages. Blueprint for every exam: format, timing, pass rules, content weights. Start here.
  • Module Guide72 pages. Learning outcomes and proficiency levels for each module.
  • Accredited university programs (current program)CPA Canada’s national list of accredited programs and the CPA PEP modules each covers. A September 2023 snapshot from the Internet Archive; may be out of date.
  • Competency Map 2.032 pages. The 2022 map the program is built on.

02 · Sample exams

  • Knowledge Assessment sample questions
  • Foundational Development sample questions
  • Exam 1 · Common, case 1: Quartz Construction
  • Exam 1 · Common, case 2: Mont Bellevue Academy
  • Exam 1 · Licensure Part B: Seaway Property Management
  • Exam 2 · Leadership: SleepNest
  • Exam 3, case 1: ClearView Canada Foundation
  • Exam 3, case 2: Academic Prowess

03 · Ontario (CPA Ontario)

  • Regulation 9-3: CPA Professional Program35 pages. The binding rules: registration, modules, exams, attempts, experience, accredited pathways.
  • Regulation 9-4: Student Transition7 pages. Final legacy dates, automatic transition dates, exemption table.
  • CPA Professional Program Policies63 pages. How the regulation is applied: transcripts, attempts, work experience, mentors, training offices.
  • Regulation 17-1: Public Accounting LicensingChargeable-hour requirements for a licence.

04 · West (CPAWSB)

  • Education and Experience Policies (draft, May 2026)43 pages. The fullest rulebook published by any region.
  • Transition Policies for Current Candidates (Oct 20, 2026)12 pages. Placement table, experience mapping, extra time.
  • Start-date timeline graphic

05 · Quebec (Ordre des CPA du Québec)

  • Calendar of both programs, 2027–2029 (French)Which modules are offered each session, and each “last time offered”.
  • Transition table (French)
  • New versus current program comparison
  • New program structure · current program structure
  • Launch timeline, Order program · universities

06 · Atlantic (CPA Atlantic School of Business)

  • Transition Policy for Current Candidates15 pages. Includes worked scenarios combining education, exams, experience and time limits.
